title: Subject-Verb Agreement
summary: The rules for making verbs agree with their subjects, including tricky subjects such as everyone, neither... nor, one of and there is or there are, with common mistakes and practice with answers.

blocks.text: The **verb must agree with its subject** in number: a **singular** subject takes a singular verb, a **plural** subject takes a plural verb. The bus **leaves** at eight. The buses **leave** at eight.

In the present simple, a singular verb usually ends in **-s** (she runs, it works), which is the opposite of nouns, where **-s** usually means plural. Agreement errors are among the most common mistakes in student writing, so checking them is a quick way to protect your grammar mark.

headers: Singular subject (he / she / it / one thing)
Plural subject (we / you / they / two or more)

blocks.text: Remember: I takes am and was, and you always takes the plural form (you are, you were), even for one person.

rows: Singular subject → singular verb, plural → plural
The bus leaves at eight. The buses leave at eight.
Ignore phrases between the subject and verb
The box of old photographs was in the attic. (subject = box)
Two subjects joined by and → plural
Salma and her brother are here.
either... or / neither... nor → verb agrees with the nearer subject
Neither the teacher nor the students were ready. / Neither the students nor the teacher was ready.
each, every, everyone, nobody, someone → singular
Everyone is welcome. Each of the rooms has a balcony.
as well as / along with do not make the subject plural
The captain, as well as the players, was tired.
Amounts of money, time and distance as one unit → singular
Ten kilometres is too far to walk.
Collective nouns: singular as one unit
The team is in the final.
There is / There are: agree with the noun after
There are many reasons. There is one reason.
One of my friends lives in Alexandria.
A number of students have complained.
The number of visitors has doubled.
Nouns ending in -s that are one subject: news, maths, physics, economics
The news is good. Maths is my favourite subject.
Pair nouns: trousers, scissors, glasses, jeans
My glasses are on the table. (but A pair of glasses is...)
Great Expectations is a long novel.
Here / There at the start: the subject comes after the verb
Here are your tickets. There was a loud noise.
agree with the noun the relative pronoun refers to
She is the student who wins every race. These are the books that belong to me.

blocks.title: Find the real subject
blocks.text: Cover the words between the subject and the verb (phrases with of, with, in, as well as, including). Then read the subject and verb together: The list (of names) **is** on the door.

rows: The price of the tickets are too high.
The price of the tickets is too high.
Everyone in the class have a laptop.
Everyone in the class has a laptop.
One of the boys were hurt.
One of the boys was hurt.
My friend and her sister is coming.
My friend and her sister are coming.
Two subjects joined by and = plural.

blocks.text: Agreement is **rarely asked about by name** in reading. It matters mostly in **your writing**: every agreement mistake is an accuracy error, and several of them pull your grammar mark down. It may also appear in proofreading-style tasks, where you correct a sentence or choose the right form.

**In your writing**, take extra care with long subjects (The number of cars on our streets **is** rising), with everyone / each / every, with There is / There are, and with was / were. Check these during your final proofread.

blocks.title: الفاعل والفعل
items: الفاعل المفرد: is / was / has / does والفعل بياخد s في المضارع.
الفاعل الجمع: are / were / have / do والفعل من غير s.
everyone و each و every و nobody مفرد دايمًا: everyone is.
One of the students مفرد عشان الفاعل هو one، و There are مع الجمع.

items.q: Choose: The basket of oranges (was / were) on the table.
Choose: Neither the players nor the coach (was / were) happy.
items.a: **was**: the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the coach.

items.q: Choose: Each of the students (has / have) a locker.
Choose: There (is / are) three reasons why I disagree.
items.a: **are**: the noun after it, reasons, is plural.

items.q: Choose: Physics (is / are) my hardest subject.
items.a: **is**: physics is one subject, so it is singular.

items.q: Choose: A number of parents (has / have) written to the school.
items.a: **have**: a number of means many, so it is plural.

items.q: Correct: One of my cousins live in Canada.
items.a: One of my cousins lives in Canada. (the subject is one)

items.q: Correct: The children, as well as their teacher, was excited.
items.a: The children, as well as their teacher, were excited. (the subject is the children, plural)

items.q: Find and correct the two agreement errors: Everybody in my family love football, and my brothers watches every match.
items.a: Everybody in my family **loves** football, and my brothers **watch** every match.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: Find the real subject, then match the verb. and = plural. each / every / everyone = singular. There is / are agrees with the noun after it. one of the... = singular.
